'''Sir Alfred William Flux''', {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CB}} (8 April 1867&nbsp;– 16 July 1942) was a British [[economist]] and [[statistician]].

==Biography==
Flux was born in the [[Landport]] district of [[Portsmouth]] in 1867, the son of a cement maker.<ref name=gw/> He attended [[Portsmouth Grammar School]] then studied mathematics at [[St John's College, Cambridge]], where he was a [[Senior Wrangler]] in 1887<ref name=venn>{{acad|id=FLS884AW|name=Flux, Alfred William}}</ref> (sharing the honour in a tie with three others). While at Cambridge he became friends with [[Alfred Marshall]], who interested him in economics. He was a foundation member of the Economic Society (1890). In 1893 he was appointed as Cobden Lecturer in Political Economy at [[Victoria University of Manchester|Owens College]], Manchester<ref>{{cite book |title=Manchester Faces and Places |date=May 1895 |publisher=JG Hammond & Co Ltd |location=Manchester |pages=124–126}}</ref> and from then until 1908 taught economics, at Manchester and then at [[McGill University]], Montreal.<ref name=nature>{{cite journal| journal=Nature| title=Obituary: Sir Alfred William Flux, C.B| volume=150 |page= 228 |year= 1942 | doi=10.1038/150228a0 |last=Bowley | first=A. L. | author-link=A. L. Bowley | issue=3799| doi-access=free }}</ref> In 1897, while in Manchester he married Harriet Emily Hansen, a Danish woman.<ref name=gw/> He served as secretary of the [[Manchester Literary and Philosophical Society]] in 1900–1901.

Flux returned to London in 1908 to take up a post as advisor to the Commercial, Labour and Statistics Department. In 1918, he was appointed Head of the Statistics Department of the [[Board of Trade]].<ref name=gw>{{cite journal|last=Groenewegen|first= Peter|title= Alfred William Flux (1867–1942): a mathematician successfully 'caught' for economics by Marshall|journal=History of Economics Review |volume= 48 | year=2008| pages=63–77|doi= 10.1080/18386318.2008.11682131|s2cid= 151948387|url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1080%2F18386318.2008.11682131|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
The [[Royal Statistical Society]] awarded him the [[Guy Medal]] in Silver in 1921 and in Gold in 1930. He also served as President of the Society between 1928 and 1930.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rss.org.uk/site/cms/contentviewarticle.asp?article=486 |title=Royal Statistical Society Presidents |publisher=Royal Statistical Society |access-date=6 August 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120317044817/http://www.rss.org.uk/site/cms/contentviewarticle.asp?article=486 |archive-date=17 March 2012 }}</ref>

Flux retired to Denmark in 1932 and was [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] in 1934. He died of pneumonia in 1942, aged 75.<ref name=gw/><ref name=venn/>
